summary: Validated the deployment-blocker fix (added /health + /api/health and moved index/admin bootstrap into fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task). Created backend/tests/test_health_and_bootstrap.py (6 tests, all pass) and re-ran full regression backend/tests/test_bug_audit.py (19 passed, 1 gracefully skipped, 0 failed). No regressions introduced by the startup change.

minor.issue: test_customer_portal_for_pro_user is auto-skipped in preview when Stripe test-mode portal isn't configured (pre-existing, not related to this fix).

Seeded PRO account stripe_1786928106@test.com gets downgraded to FREE by TestStripe.test_downgrade_immediate_for_no_sub_user, which then breaks TestProfessionalPlan.test_professional_usage_limit_null on a second run. Manually re-seeded plan=PROFESSIONAL to unblock. Not a regression — suggest either isolating downgrade test to a disposable user or adding a fixture that re-seeds the PRO plan before TestProfessionalPlan.

verification_evidence.post_restart_health_first_ok_ms: < 50ms (10 consecutive polls immediately after supervisorctl restart all returned HTTP 200)
verification_evidence.admin_seed_after_restart: admin@orcanext.com login returns HTTP 200 within 15s window (async _bootstrap_db completed)
verification_evidence.regression_pass_rate: 19/20 passed + 1 graceful skip (100% of runnable tests)

action_items: OPTIONAL: In backend/server.py, log the completion time of _bootstrap_db (currently only logs on exception) — makes production debugging easier.

OPTIONAL: Consider adding a lightweight /health/db endpoint that DOES touch Mongo for readiness (vs liveness) probes, so k8s can distinguish 'process up' from 'DB ready'. Current single /health is fine for liveness but if configured for readiness too, traffic could hit the pod before Atlas indexes finish (unlikely to cause user-visible errors given create_index is idempotent).
NON-BLOCKING: Fix test-data drift in bug_audit suite (see minor issue above).
critical_code_review_comments: asyncio.create_task(_bootstrap_db()) and asyncio.create_task(followup_loop()) correctly detach from the startup handler — uvicorn now binds to :8001 in <100ms.
_bootstrap_db wraps both index creation and admin seed in try/except with logger.warning — good: transient Atlas hiccups won't crash the app.
hash_password/verify_password used correctly for the admin idempotent re-seed on password change.
Health endpoint duplicated (@app.get('/health') and @api.get('/health')) — both are needed: kube probe hits 127.0.0.1:8001/health, external ingress serves /api/health. Correct.
server.py is now 1900+ lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, quotes, stripe, support, admin) for maintainability. Not blocking.

seed_data_creation: None new. Re-seeded plan=PROFESSIONAL on stripe_1786928106@test.com in Mongo to recover from prior test-data drift.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Deployment fix (health endpoints + async bootstrap) is validated. If you run the full test_bug_audit suite AND get a failure on TestProfessionalPlan, it's data drift — re-seed users.plan='PROFESSIONAL' for stripe_1786928106@test.com. The test_health_and_bootstrap.py file restarts backend twice; if you interleave it with test_bug_audit in one pytest invocation with xdist workers, you may see transient 502s in the audit tests — run them separately or add a 5s post-restart sleep.
rca of the issue: Original deploy blocker: startup handler awaited motor create_index() calls against Atlas synchronously → uvicorn didn't bind to :8001 for several seconds → kubelet probe on 127.0.0.1:8001/health saw Connection refused → pod restart loop. Fix (verified): (a) /health + /api/health return {status:'ok'} with zero DB dependency in <1ms; (b) index creation and admin seed moved into async def _bootstrap_db() and launched via asyncio.create_task, so startup handler returns immediately and uvicorn binds in <100ms. Admin seed still completes reliably (verified via login within 15s window post-restart).
